description:
Recall memories from AutoMem in one of three modes. The mode is selected by which params you pass.

**Mode 1 — ID fetch:** pass `memory_id` to retrieve a single memory by ID. All other params are ignored. Routes to GET /memory/{id} and updates last_accessed.

**Mode 2 — Tag enumeration:** pass `tags` + `exhaustive: true` for paginated exact-match listing (NOT ranked retrieval). Use this for cleanup/audit workflows where ranked retrieval silently undercounts large tag sets. Pair with `limit` (≤200) and `offset`. Returns `has_more`/`limit`/`offset` page metadata; next page at `next_offset`. Tag matching is exact, case-insensitive, any-of mode — `tag_match: "prefix"` and `tag_mode: "all"` are rejected in this mode.

**Mode 3 — Ranked retrieval (default):** hybrid search across vector, keyword, tags, recency, and optional graph expansion. The primary tool for finding relevant context. By default, ranked recall requests current active memories only; set `current_only: false` for audits.

**When to use ranked (mode 3):**
- At conversation start: recall context about the current project/topic
- Before making decisions: check for past decisions on similar topics
- When debugging: search for similar past errors and their solutions
- For complex questions: use `expand_entities` for multi-hop reasoning

**When to use enumeration (mode 2):** when you need to know *how many* memories carry a tag, or to walk all of them for cleanup/migration. Ranked recall ignores low-importance hits — enumeration does not.

**Examples:**
- recall_memory({ query: "database architecture decisions", tags: ["my-project"], limit: 5 })
- recall_memory({ memory_id: "8f3a2c1e-5b7d-4e9a-a1c3-2d4f6b8e0a91" })  // Mode 1
- recall_memory({ tags: ["benchmark-test"], exhaustive: true, limit: 50 })  // Mode 2 (add offset for later pages)
- recall_memory({ query: "auth", exclude_tags: ["deprecated"] })  // Mode 3 with exclusion
- recall_memory({ query: "What is Sarah's sister's job?", expand_entities: true })  // Mode 3 multi-hop

active_path.description: Current file path, for language detection.

adaptive_floor.description: Ranked-mode only. Apply the service's adaptive score floor.

auto_decompose.description: Add searches for entities and topics extracted from the query.

current_only.description: Ranked-mode only. Hide archived, not-yet-valid, expired, invalidated or superseded memories.

exhaustive.description: Tag enumeration mode: requires `tags`; exact any-of match, `limit` ≤200, pages with `offset`. Rejects `tag_match: "prefix"` and `tag_mode: "all"`.

expand_entities.description: Multi-hop: also recall memories about entities in the seed results.

expand_min_importance.description: Drop expanded results below this importance; seeds are never filtered.

expand_min_strength.description: Follow only relations at least this strong. Not used by entity expansion.

expand_relations.description: Follow graph relations from seed results.

expand_respect_tags.description: Ranked-mode only. Keep graph/entity expansion inside the tag scope.

format.description: text, items (one block per memory) and detailed (adds type, confidence, metadata keys, relation stubs) show a 400-char content preview; fetch the full record by memory_id. json returns full fields. Every format stays within the response token budget.

limit.description: Defaults to 5 in ranked mode and 20 in enumeration mode. Ranked is clamped to ~50 server-side.

memory_id.description: ID fetch mode: returns this one memory and ignores every other param.

offset.description: Enumeration mode only (`exhaustive: true`). Ranked recall rejects it; raise `limit` instead.

recency_bias.description: Ranked-mode only. "auto" lets the service decide.

scope_fallback.description: Ranked-mode only. Fill from outside the tag scope when scoped evidence is weak.

state_debug.description: Ranked-mode only. Add suppression IDs and reasons to `state_filter`.

state_mode.description: Ranked-mode only. "history" includes superseded/invalidated memories. Prefer over current_only.

tag_match.description: "prefix" (ranked default) also matches child tags split at ":" or "/" (`auth` matches `auth:login`); it does not match across hyphens. "exact" matches whole tags. Enumeration mode is always exact.

tags.description: Filter by tags, e.g. the project slug.

name: recall_memory

has_more.description: Enumeration: more records exist; continue at `next_offset`.

limit.description: Enumeration: page size. A budget-trimmed page shrinks `count` and `limit` to what was returned, so `offset + limit` still starts the next page.

next_offset.description: Enumeration, while `has_more`: the next page offset.

content.description: A preview outside json and ID fetch.

content_truncated.description: Content is a preview; fetch the full record by memory_id.

deduped_from.description: IDs merged into this result by multi-query dedup.

state_replaces.description: ID of the suppressed memory this result replaced.

t_invalid.description: json and ID fetch only; set when superseded.

state_filter.description: Counts; IDs and reasons only with state_debug.

truncation.description: Present when the response budget cut anything: applied, omitted_results, reason, omitted_fields (diagnostics dropped), compacted_results (json results shown compact).

title: Recall Memory
